execution_engine.not_matlab_caveat: MATLAB execution in this project is documented BOOTSTRAP-ONLY (scripts/matlab/README.md), requiring a human-driven MATLAB Online session; that pathway was not used here. This is NOT because Karr/WholeCell source is unavailable: the full upstream WholeCell source tree (including the complete Simulation classdef object graph and RandStream.m) IS present locally at E:\opencell-mirrors\WholeCell (a mirror/junction outside this git worktree). The isolated per-process harness approach below was a deliberate tractability choice, not a source-availability workaround: replaying the original extract_per_process_traces_v2.m pattern requires instantiating and fitting a full Simulation object via the KnowledgeBase construction pipeline, which is a heavyweight, long-running MATLAB-only process not reproducible from this sandboxed session in Octave. Both target code paths, however, are isolable without that full object graph (see scripts/octave_h12_perturbation/README.md), so this harness runs the VERBATIM vendored Karr .m logic (function bodies transcribed unmodified from data/karr_vendored_source/*.m) with only the WholeCell RandStream/base-Process classdef scaffolding replaced by minimal harness stubs, documented per-scenario below. The real edu.stanford.covert.util.RandStream.m source (E:\opencell-mirrors\WholeCell\src\+edu\+stanford\+covert\+util\RandStream.m, method stochasticRound, line 236) was read and confirmed to match this harness's stochasticRoundStub.m formula exactly (roundUp = rand < mod(value,1); ceil if roundUp else floor); mnrnd is MATLAB's Statistics Toolbox builtin (not custom WholeCell code), and mnrndStub.m reimplements its documented multinomial-sampling semantics. Where a scenario's RNG-dependent code path IS exercised (MacromolecularComplexation network>=2), the Octave drivers seed via the legacy `rand('seed', k)` API (scripts/octave_h12_perturbation/run_macromol_network2.m) -- this is Octave/MATLAB's backward-compatible legacy seeding syntax, not an assertion that Octave's underlying generator algorithm matches MATLAB's RandStream implementation; no bit-identical RNG claim is made, so evidence from that scenario is DISTRIBUTIONAL/STRUCTURAL (invariant-checked across 50 independent seeds), never claimed as bit-exact H12 evidence. Where a scenario's perturbed values are constructed so that no fractional/RNG-consuming code path is ever reached (ProteinProcessingII Scenario A), the harness stub's specific RNG behavior is provably irrelevant to the outcome, so exact-match H12 evidence IS claimed for that one constructed regime only (see caveats in the generated artifacts).

scenario_b_execution_engine.tool: Genuine local MATLAB (NOT Octave) plus the Statistics Toolbox, invoked directly on the developer's machine -- NOT the project's bootstrap-only MATLAB Online pathway (scripts/matlab/README.md), and NOT the GNU Octave harness `execution_engine` block above (that block continues to describe Scenario A and macromol-network2 unchanged).
scenario_b_execution_engine.why_not_octave: Octave has no `RandStream` class of the shape Karr's edu.stanford.covert.util.RandStream.m wraps, and no Statistics-Toolbox `mnrnd`/`binornd`/`poissrnd`. scripts/octave_h12_perturbation/mnrndStub.m and stochasticRoundStub.m are explicitly-documented non-Karr scaffolds; Opus5's turn-3 review held that using them as 'evidence' for the dormant transferase/scarcity branch's real stochastic behavior would not be valid evidence for that branch (the whole point of Scenario B), even though the same stubs remain valid for Scenario A (there, they are provably irrelevant no-ops) and for macromol-network2 (there, only distributional/structural invariants are claimed, and legacy `rand('seed', k)` reseeding is explicitly NOT claimed bit-identical to MATLAB's RandStream).
scenario_b_execution_engine.randstream_provenance: The runtime WholeCell src/ root (containing +edu/+stanford/+covert/+util/RandStream.m) is resolved ONLY via an explicit --wholecell-src-root CLI argument or the OPENCELL_WHOLECELL_SRC_ROOT environment variable (scripts/l22_evidence/h12_perturbation.py::_resolve_wholecell_src_root) -- there is NO ambient/hardcoded default path (Opus5 turn-4 correction 2; a prior design silently assumed data/m1_sources/WholeCell/src, a path that does not exist in this repo). The resolved root is passed to MATLAB via the PPII_WHOLECELL_SRC_ROOT environment variable, which both probe_matlab_environment.m and run_ppii_scenario_b_matlab.m read via getenv(...) before addpath(...)-ing it. Both scripts record `which('edu.stanford.covert.util.RandStream')` (the actual resolved file path) and an LF-normalized SHA-256 hash of that file in their JSON output (probe result / per-state run-manifest respectively); scripts/l22_evidence/h12_perturbation.py independently re-verifies that hash against the vendored flat copy at data/karr_vendored_source/RandStream.m (pinned upstream commit 6cdee6b355aa0f5ff2953b1ab356eea049108e07) and raises if they do not match -- this is a cross-check performed by Python, never a bare self-report trusted from MATLAB. The vendored copy itself is never added to the MATLAB path or executed; it exists purely as the audit/hash-pinning baseline.
scenario_b_execution_engine.no_stub_fallback: scripts/matlab_h12_perturbation/run_ppii_scenario_b_matlab.m ABORTS (raises a MATLAB error, writes no output) if: running under Octave, the PPII_WHOLECELL_SRC_ROOT environment variable is unset, the Statistics Toolbox is unlicensed or not installed, edu.stanford.covert.util.RandStream cannot be found on the path, or a RandStream instance cannot be constructed. There is no code path that substitutes a stub/scaffold RNG when the real one is unavailable. scripts/matlab_h12_perturbation/probe_matlab_environment.m performs the same checks read-only, in isolation, before any evidentiary run is attempted, PLUS an independent `mnrnd(3, [0.5;0.5])` column-vector shape probe (Opus5 turn-4 correction 1 -- see `mnrnd_shape_probe` below); it writes a structured JSON result unconditionally (even on failure) and calls MATLAB's `error(...)` if `overall_pass` is false, so both the process exit code and the JSON result agree that the environment is unready. scripts/l22_evidence/h12_perturbation.py's `probe_matlab_environment()`/`run_matlab_scenario_b()` never trust a bare exit code alone -- they always load and independently re-validate this JSON (Opus5 turn-4 correction 3).
scenario_b_execution_engine.mnrnd_shape_probe: evolveState_ppii_matlab.m calls `this.randStream.mnrnd(n, columnVector)'` VERBATIM -- i.e. a COLUMN vector `p` is passed straight through to RandStream.mnrnd, itself a thin passthrough to the builtin `mnrnd` with no shape correction (data/karr_vendored_source/RandStream.m lines 127-137). probe_matlab_environment.m therefore runs a synthetic `mnrnd(3, [0.5;0.5])` probe under genuine MATLAB and records `mnrnd_shape_test_status` as 'pass' or 'error'. A 'pass' permits later full-mode consideration (combined with `overall_pass`); an 'error' is recorded as a genuine Karr dormant-source defect and HARD-BLOCKS full-mode execution only -- it is NOT fixed post hoc in evolveState_ppii_matlab.m (that file's exact shape is the whole point of the probe), and it does NOT block canary-mode plumbing runs (Opus5 turn-4 correction 1).

shared_derivation_notes.index_reuse: All 5 states reuse the SAME fixture-real index arrays as Scenario A (lipoproteinMonomerIndexs_0b, secretedMonomerIndexs_0b), populating only their first 3 (lipoprotein) and first 4 (secreted) slots per state; all other monomer slots (including all 3 passthrough indices used by Scenario A) are held at 0 in every Scenario B state, since passthrough_fires is not this scenario's target and is already covered by both the natural trace and Scenario A.
shared_derivation_notes.rate_constants_used: lipoproteinSignalPeptidaseSpecificRate=11.0, lipoproteinDiacylglycerylTransferaseSpecificRate=0.0165, stepSizeSec=1.0 -- all REAL fixture constants (ProteinProcessingII_flat.mat), unchanged from Scenario A and from the natural trace; never perturbed by any Scenario B state.
shared_derivation_notes.capacity_formulas: peptidase_limit = enzymes_signalPeptidase * 11.0 * 1.0; transferase_limit = enzymes_diacylglycerylTransferase * 0.0165 * 1.0 -- identical closed-form used by the accepted, unmodified predict_protein_processing_ii (scripts/l22_evidence/h12.py), so each state's intended guard-failure reason is mechanically cross-checked (not just hand-derived) by the pre-existing predictor.
shared_derivation_notes.margin_policy: Every scarce guard is failed with a margin (not at the exact integer boundary) to avoid a state whose PASS/FAIL regime could flip due to floating-point or stochasticRound boundary sensitivity; every passing guard is passed with a margin for the same reason. The one deliberately near-fair-coin fractional part per state (see each state's `hand_traced_mechanics`) is the sole exception, chosen BECAUSE it is near 0.5, specifically to make cross-seed stochasticRound variation robustly observable in only 50 draws -- this is choosing a value to make the STOCHASTIC MECHANISM legible, not to fit a predicted outcome (no outcome is predicted at the per-species point level; see evidence_contract).

exact_zero_tolerance_claims: mass_conservation: sum(unprocessedMonomers_after) + sum(processedMonomers_after) == sum(unprocessedMonomers_before) for every seed, exactly. (There is no separate 'passthrough pool' array in this invariant: evolveState_ppii_matlab.m moves mass directly between unprocessedMonomers and processedMonomers only -- signalSequenceMonomers is a side-channel bookkeeping array Karr's code also increments for signal-peptide-cleaved species, not a third mass-conservation pool, and substrates (water/PG160/SNGLYP/hydrogen) are consumed/produced by a disjoint balance evaluate_ppii_scarcity_invariants checks separately as pool_cap_peptidase/pool_cap_transferase below, not folded into this monomer-mass identity.)
non_negativity: every post-state species count and every pool count >= 0, for every seed, exactly.

per_species_cap: processed_count(species) <= unprocessedMonomers_before(species), for every seed and species, exactly (stochasticRound/mnrnd can only reallocate/round DOWN from raw demand at the species actually processed, never invent monomer mass).

pool_cap_peptidase: sum(final_transformations(peptidaseIndexs)) <= substrates_water_before, for every seed, exactly -- proved unconditionally in the pre-registration's derivation appendix (see H12 turn-1 intent, part C) from the min(rounded_transformations, mnrnd_draw) clamping structure and mnrnd's exact-sum-to-n multinomial identity; holds regardless of which stochastic path (mnrnd firing or not) is realized.

pool_cap_transferase: sum(final_transformations(transferaseIndexs)) <= substrates_PG160_before, for every seed, exactly -- same proof structure as pool_cap_peptidase, applied to the PG160/transferase side.
distributional_only_claims: species_allocation: the exact per-species processed count for any species subject to stochasticRound (non-integer scaled demand) or mnrnd (pool below aggregate demand) is NOT claimed as an exact point prediction -- only that it lies in the algebraic bound above, and that it is observed to VARY across the pre-registered independent seeds for at least one species in every state whose `hand_traced_mechanics` names a firing stochastic mechanism (this is the cross-seed-variation requirement: mnrnd/stochasticRound must not degenerate into a no-op across the seed schedule, which would silently launder a deterministic scenario as stochastic evidence).
evidence_contract.anti_laundering_boundary: Predictions (predict_ppii_scarcity_bounds) are computed from `states_before`-only pre-registered inputs and PERSISTED TO DISK (freeze_ppii_scenario_b_predictions writes one ppii_scenario_b_<name>_prediction.json per state, hash-binding the corresponding generated state file) during generate-inputs-scenario-b, strictly BEFORE any MATLAB process is invoked. The MATLAB driver (run_ppii_scenario_b_matlab.m) reads this same frozen file only for its pre-registered seed list and state-file staleness check -- it never writes or alters the prediction. The ingest/comparison phase (ingest_ppii_scenario_b) LOADS this frozen JSON file and compares it against the MATLAB-produced `states_after` CSV plus that CSV's own run-manifest; it never recomputes the prediction after raw MATLAB output exists, never reads the OC SUT, never a runner, and never any oracle-after value from the natural trace. This mirrors the existing PREDICT_PHASE_FUNCTIONS/COMPARE_PHASE_FUNCTIONS AST-import-guard split already enforced for Scenario A and MacromolecularComplexation network2 by tests/scripts/test_h12_perturbation.py.

water_scarce.derivation: enzymes: REAL fixture-constant values (unperturbed, same as Scenario A / natural trace). secreted demand [20,15,10,5] (sum=50): chosen so peptidase_demand(50) is comfortably below peptidase_limit=58*11=638 (guard passes) while comfortably exceeding substrates_water=30 (guard fails) -- isolates the water guard as the sole failure cause. lipoprotein all 0 (transferase_demand=0) so the transferase/PG160 guards are trivially satisfied and block1 (transferase-side scaling) never executes, keeping this state's stochastic mechanism isolated to the water-side mnrnd re-allocation in block2.
water_scarce.hand_traced_mechanics: block1 skipped (no lipoprotein unprocessed monomers); block2: peptidaseLimit=638 (unreduced) >= demand(50), so stochasticRound scaling is a no-op (scale=1, all integer inputs); sum(transformations)=50 > water(30), so mnrnd(30, [20,15,10,5]/50) FIRES -- this state exercises mnrnd only, not stochasticRound. NOT the canary state (corrected per Opus5 turn-3 review: this state never enters block1/the transferase branch at all, since transferase_demand=0 here, so it cannot serve as evidence that the transferase branch fires -- see transferase_capacity_scarce below, which is now the designated canary).

pg160_scarce.derivation: enzymes: REAL fixture-constant values (unperturbed). lipoprotein demand [3,1,1] (sum=5): peptidase_demand=5 << peptidase_limit=638 (passes); transferase_demand=5 << transferase_limit=372*0.0165=6.138 (passes with margin); water=1000 >> 5 (passes). substrates_PG160=3 < transferase_demand(5): the ONE deliberately failed guard, isolating PG160 as the sole failure cause.
